steps.text: Slowly, the life pod opens.
There, you see a familiar face, just as you have hoped to see thousands of times.
Once again, you take her hand.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}?
Slowly, the woman inside gets up.

steps.name: Amiya/Mon3tr
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit! / Kal'tsit!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I did it?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Woohoo, I did it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Kal'tsit, is that you? Do you recognize me? If not, you gotta at least recognize the Doctor and Amiya, right?

Amiya suppresses the urge to dash forward to embrace Kal'tsit, as Mon3tr digs her sharp claws deep into the soil beneath. Each and every one of them looks on nervously, as not one of them can so easily believe this outcome.
In contrast, the woman who has just been roused from her slumber looks to each member of the group gathered around her. Slowly, her bewildered expression begins to soften.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Somebody tell me... Why am I here?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's all thanks to the Doctor—and Closure, too!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We've been racking our brains to recreate the gemini cycle function and use blank Originium to sculpt a body for you!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: The experiments haven't been going well, but somehow, we managed to find AMa-10's source code in the Sarcophagus in Ursus—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's practically impossible, in theory...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doesn't matter!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Well... Are you feeling okay? Are your memories all jumbled? And, um—

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Do you still remember me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How could I ever forget you...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I really missed you...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Watch out, Mon3tr! Dr. Kal'tsit may still be very weak!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you, Amiya...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Don't worry... I can tell... my condition isn't particularly serious.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What I really want to know is... where are we, and what is the current situation?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (Pants weakly)

options: You don't need to be in such a hurry to figure out what's going on.
Don't push yourself. We still have time.
I don't want you to worry...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I must say... I really do not agree with how you led Rhodes Island... on such a dangerous operation.

options: We need you to come back to fight alongside us.
Amiya and I arrived at this decision together.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, I've never doubted your decisions for a long time. However...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm afraid I'll have to reevaluate your decision-making now.

options: I'll get your whole critique once we're back at Rhodes Island.
Naturally, I had other reasons too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: For example?

options: Have you found yourself yet... Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I never forgot.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I hear fighting... I suppose Ursus's many factions are still vying for the Sarcophagus?

options: This does indeed have to do with the Sarcophagus.
The situation is a little more complicated than that.
We should get ready to pull out.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I need to know... where is the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I still have... unfinished business.
After stopping in front of the bloody palm print on the door for a brief moment, the man starts to slowly walk out of the dark corridor.
The only energy pipeline from the satellite city has begun to operate once more. He has fulfilled his promise.
Nothing following that is of any importance to him.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Alita...
The man slowly falls to his knees and picks up one of the countless ice-cold bodies on the floor.
Had you long since given up the ideals that you talked about as a girl, when you fed fowlbeasts by the pond, would you really have ended up like this?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I never had the courage to tell you... I'd actually completely forgotten the promises I made before the statues of our forebears... those lies I told for the empire's sake.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: And I've never really cared about their so-called 'better tomorrow.'

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: All I know is that, when a soldier leaves home, his family is always there to send him off, yet when we left Chernobog, the entire city was still asleep.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: For so many days and nights, all I've wanted is to go back to Lada's bedside.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: But I had to keep an eye on you, too.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I have to look after you... so you won't be alone... chasing things and hurting yourself in the process.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Hah...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Klim Valuev... In the end...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: You still managed to accomplish nothing.

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: All clear...

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: The bodies...
Found a survivor.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Who are you people?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Never mind. Doesn't matter.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: If you're here for the Sarcophagus. It's right behind me.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: If that's not what you are after...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Then get out. Now.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: Assessment complete.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: The Sarcophagus weaponization module has been completely destroyed. Only its energy transformation stabilizer module remains, with an external channel still operational.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: The Sarcophagus's core structure is massive and complex. It is nigh impossible to neatly dismantle for transportation with such little time. Please advise.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: Right, it's irreparable. It cannot be done, even with all of us deploying the strongest evocation-conversion Arts at once.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: The weaponization module's damage appears to have been caused by some sort of even greater power.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: Furthermore, based on observations prior to entry, the plate housing the Sarcophagus has suffered continual external attack. We can surmise that the First Army has already abandoned Zelgrad.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: Acknowledged.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: We'll pull out immediately.
From afar, the soldiers, having just received their orders, look upon the sole survivor.
The sound of explosions outside is drawing ever closer, yet it seems he is making no effort to escape at all.
Why waste time on a man who will not live?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: This is the last time. Forgive my cowardice, Alita.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: After all... you've always been the bravest of us.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Even the Second Army... Even the Second Army has turned against me, Witte!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What are we waiting for? For the traitors to march into Grypherburg and Tsarevgrad—for them to breach the palace and impale me on the throne?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty... You must know why the Second Army resorted to such means.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: The Winter Emergency Resource Allocation Act.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: They think this bill will inevitably hurt their interests, perhaps even the Army's authority independent of the legislature. That's why they chose to turn a blind eye to the Fourth Army's actions.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No... Even suppose they had a problem with that, they wouldn't have gone against the edict like this... Someone must be fanning the flames!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Is it her... or who else would it be? My dear aunt...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Majesty... All things considered, our top priority should be the crisis at hand.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: That said, each day that this bill isn't passed is another day that the Second Army doesn't point their spears directly to Grypherburg.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Therefore, strictly speaking, they have yet to form any kind of coalition of mutual interest, and we still have a chance to negotiate with the Second Army.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Moreover—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Witte, Witte! Listen to yourself. What nonsense are you talking?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Even a traitor like Saveliy knows that the Second Army's decision to stand on the sidelines is tantamount to rebellion against us, and you're still making excuses for them.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: If I didn't know you and trust you, such words would be enough to brand you a traitor like the rest of them!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: If such thinking calms your nerves, then fine, but I also know that you are no tyrant. You want to solve real problems, not emotional ones.

spans.text: If such thinking calms your nerves, then fine, but I also know that you are no tyrant. You want to solve

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Which is why, no matter how furious you may be, you still have that basic level of sanity. You are not like those wild beasts.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What will you do, Witte? Will you really accede to their demands and postpone the citizen's forum indefinitely?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: No, Majesty, I won't. The final deadline that we gave them is tomorrow's citizen's forum.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: If, before the citizen's forum is called, we fail to cut a deal with the Second Army, make no progress on the Sarcophagus's energy, and the Grand Duchess doesn't change her position...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Then we will have no choice but to mobilize the Central Army and stop all these sides from coming to blows, and at the same time put a stop to all this sedition once and for all... There will be no mercy or patience.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Even if none of us know whether the empire can still withstand a civil war of such scale.
Within the fire burns the final urgent letter from the south.
Before the flames can reach her fingertips, Elisaveta lets go of the letter and pulls back her hand.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: So the Second Army chose to stand on the sidelines too?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Although this development is hardly unexpected.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: It's just that the Chairman may have to play his very last card.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: My merciful, fledgling, and pitiful liege... Within you flows the blood of the old Tsar, yet unlike your father, you are not fit to be autocrat of all the Ursines.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Nor is there an advisor at your side, as capable as the late Empress was.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: If all you're doing is pushing things through, how long can you possibly last?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: It's a good thing, then, that an individual more suited to the job has returned...
Her gaze turns to a woman looking at a painting on the wall.
Her features are practically the same as those of a woman in the portrait.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Auntie.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Is this... a painting of me?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: No, my love. That is your mother. Your father, too.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: It seems I have forgotten their smiles.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: It's a cruel side effect that sometimes comes with the pains of life, not to mention that you've been through far too much these past few years.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: But I must remember.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: You will. I will help you... I will always help you, and stand by your side.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Ever since you were a child, you have been strong and unwilling to concede defeat. You are far too much like your father.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: My father... What was he like?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: A ruler with excellent foresight, ambition, gallantry. He poured his heart and soul into revitalizing Ursus's territorial expansion and feeding his citizens, never resting even a moment until his death.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: One could say that he was the greatest man to ever grace Ursus, second only to Igor Velikiy, who forged this empire.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: He sounds very... distant.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Right, he was extraordinarily hard to get close to. Only your mother ever dared to stand near him.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Really? That sounds very lonely.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: ...I doubt he ever felt that way, other than when your mother passed—

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Auntie, what's wrong?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Let's talk about something else, Nastya.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Do you want to go back to Grypherburg?

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Grypherburg...
A hesitant expression, one that Elisaveta is all too familiar with, appears on Anastasia's face. After a brief moment, she speaks her will.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I want to see Fedya.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Fyodor, my little brother.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I want to see him.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: If I must return to Grypherburg to see him, then I wish to go back.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: If he is not there, then I will go to where he is.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: No matter where he is?

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Yes, no matter where he is.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: And why do you wish to see him?

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Must I have a special reason? I think he probably wants to see me, too.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: If that is the case, Anastasia, then you must know a certain truth first.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I am listening.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: While you were missing... no, wandering all over Ursus, Fyodor succeeded your father and tried his best to be a good Tsar.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Unfortunately, he is simply no good at it, and the job is not a good fit for him either.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: If memory serves, he loves reading, and he even wrote his own poems. Does he still do that?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: His role as the Tsar has no doubt consumed a significant majority of his time. Even if he still does write, it is most likely satirical poems written to vent his anger.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: That is just conjecture, though.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: It has been a very long time since he spoke to me. Even his letters are penned by others on his behalf.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: It seems that he hasn't changed at all... He worries about how others see him, too much for his own good.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: My poor Fedya. I can practically imagine how hard he pushes himself to become an unbiased—even ruthless—symbol... because that is what the people want.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: But he should never show that facade to you, of all people. After all, you are the only family we have, and we used to be so close... Right?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: That was a long time ago.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: There have since been certain things that I handled in a less than satisfactory way, even if it was all out of concern for him. The saddest thing is that we share the same name and should be helping one another.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Instead, he trusted an outsider, and one from the bottom rung of society with no foresight, to the point that he dragged all of Ursus into a terrible mess.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Now, this great land faces a hopeless future because of his reckless actions.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: If he would turn away a loyal family member and subject like myself at this perilous juncture... then how many do you think still stand by his side?

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: ...I understand now.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: What do you want me to do?

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Save him, and save Ursus, my dear Nastya.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: You are the only one. Only you can do this.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Because... within you flows his blood.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I should never have doubted your loyalty, my dear Witte.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: But if worse comes to worst, as you said, then you'll have to forgive my stubbornness, as I will have to take to the front lines.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: My most loyal men will be fighting for me, and with the Second Army turning against me, that is the most effective way to rouse my people.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty!

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Trust me, Witte. After all, I'm not like those weak tin soldiers in the fortress. I am—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: The Emperor and Autocrat of All the Ursines.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: Your Imperial Highness, we have news from the Deity Grypherburg Power Dispatch Center.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What have they discovered?

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: They say that the high-voltage fencing's isolated failure points have been restored. Once the transformer is in place, we will be able to use the node to restore power to some of the affected areas.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Which line did the failures originate in?

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: The lines connected to the newly built energy pipeline. That said, the power facilities are old.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: They were originally intended for use only while the city was stationary, but the lines failed not too long ago, so we temporarily isolated the failure points for investigation. They have been restored now.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Thank you. You are excused.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: It's better than nothing, but can this tiny bit of energy really feed the entire empire?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: No... This is a sign, Majesty.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: One that tells us the worst is yet to come.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Shh. She's asleep. Please, try not to wake her...
(In Sami) So, you got yourself involved.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: I know what I am getting myself into.
(In Sami) Says everyone who is willingly deceived.
(In Sami) Despite appearances, its heart is completely empty. Everything you hear and see is a mere projection of your desires.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: If you are really worried, then stay here and help me.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Use your Shaman eyes to help me see through this darkness.
(In Sami) No, that is not part of our deal.
(In Sami) The ritual is complete. I shall take my leave.
(In Sami) Before your vulgar and stupid desires backfire on you, do not forget to fulfill your end of the bargain.

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Main forces... retreating...

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: This is your final order... Eliminate... Infected creatures—

steps.name: Ursine Soldier
steps.text: Acknowledged.

steps.name: Ursine Soldier
steps.text: Staying behind to clean up again...
The soldier tosses his communicator to the side and takes a swig of vodka.
This morning, while he was kneading dough in the field kitchen, he found himself dragged outside by his officer.
This wasn't his first time using Originium bolts, but it was his first time taking a life, even if it was a mutated animal.
Before he left, he stuffed all the spirits he had into his backpack. Ever since, every time he's fired a bolt, he's taken a swig. It is the only way to keep his fingers from shaking.
A cloudbeast, or perhaps something that resembled a cloudbeast.
He thinks back to how the fluffy little things would hop into the kitchen and tug on his pants with their claws, and he would tear off a chunk of bread in exchange for a chance to pat their heads.

steps.name: Ursine Soldier
steps.text: Sorry, old friend...
He approaches the creature lying on the ground unsteadily and reaches his right hand out—
Suddenly, the creature violently bounces up and turns into a black shadow. It leaps toward the soldier, causing him to shriek and raise his arms instinctively.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Blyat! How many times have I told you?! Hold your weapon upright, get a bead on your target, then fire!

spans.text: How many times have I told you?! Hold your weapon upright, get a bead on your target, then fire!

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Once I'm done with these ublyudki, I'll drown you in your vodka!

spans.text: , I'll drown you in your vodka!

steps.text: Right after he reprimands his subordinate, despite the bolt pierced through its body, the mutated creature shrieks and leaps up again.
Before the two are able to react, a scorching hot wave blasts past them. The beast is incinerated, turned to ash, while the pavement beneath it melts into a charred black pit.

steps.name: Ursine Soldier
steps.text: Wait! You're—

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Slow down, Private. Lower your weapon. Stand aside and stay alert. I will handle her.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: He shouldn't stay here. Neither should you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: These creatures are crawling all over this city. No one should be here.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: That is not for you to decide, Reunion. My commanding officer says the area is abandoned, but I have not received orders to move out.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: And so, I cannot allow these crazed creatures to flee Zelgrad. They would go southwest and spread their disease to the people there.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Somebody has to stay... A few hundred lives for thousands more. It's a fair price to pay.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I've seen many soldiers lay down their arms during confrontation with Reunion, letting civilians leave in peace.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Were those your orders, too?

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: No, they were decisions we made on the spot. You won... temporarily, at least.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: The First Army has had losses before, but even the greenest of our soldiers stood steadfast in the face of Gaulish artillery. They waited where they stood with their stump legs for the Tsar's reinforcements.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Zelgrad belongs to the First Army... From now on, whenever Ursine citizens bring up the city, it will be known as the front line of the empire's glory, where all the monsters were quelled.

steps.name: Ursine Officer
steps.text: Which is why, if you aren't here to kill us, I ask you to let us fulfill our duty as Ursine soldiers.
The woman nods, and the old officer lowers his guard. He signals to the soldier standing nearby and walks away with him in silence.

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: You're still easily swayed by noble-sounding speeches. Perhaps that will always be your flaw, my dear...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You—!
She unsheathes her blade the moment she hears that familiar voice.
But when she turns, she finds not that familiar individual, but the ruined streets.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: The main forces have retreated.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Lyudmila, our Reunion friends are still fighting the army in the city. I can bring a few men with me to help.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Let's just leave this to them. This kind of back alley brawl is exactly Reunion's forte. Besides, you've seen how intense the battles can get in the city.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I'm not trying to sell you short... Anyone who can still hold a blade should stay to protect their friends.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Now that I've had a front-row seat to Reunion's combat style, I must say it's really quite remarkable.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: ...I haven't been one of them for a while now.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: But just to be safe, I'll be heading back to check on things and fill Red in on your situation over here.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Right. For safety's sake, I'll take everyone deeper into the forest. We'll meet up at the western boundary of the forest.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Sounds good to me.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: But before that...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I need to know who you really are.

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: Sure enough...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Ivan Tulin was an incredible warrior. If someone is taking his name, I need to know why.

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: Isn't that exactly why?

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: Ivan Tulin. This name is like a banner in the Northern Tundra. I don't want this name to disappear from the public consciousness.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You mean he's—

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: It was maybe three years ago. In the end, he wasn't able to escape the Patrol Units' manhunt.

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: I know I'm not the only person to have learned and received help from him, and I may not be the one most deserving of taking up his name. I just believe that somebody has to do it.

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: I couldn't afford to wait for somebody to step up to the task, so I did.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Perhaps Talulah will be disappointed once she learns the truth... but I believe you.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Could you at least tell me your real identity, your actual name?

steps.name: 'Tulin'
steps.text: ...Milana.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: A normal miner, the daughter of peasants.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: All my miner brothers and sisters know this, but they prefer to call me Tulin, out of habit.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: But it'd make me very happy to have a good friend willing to call me Milana.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Alright, Milana—
With a hint of remorse, Milana nods to Crownslayer, bidding her farewell.
Then, she slowly walks toward the source of the sobbing—a young girl, and some broken parts scattered across the ground.

steps.name: Ursine Boy
steps.text: Come on, Yana, don't cry. I'll help you look. We'll put it back together.

steps.name: Ursine Girl
steps.text: No... *sob*... We can't do it. Only Papa knows how.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Um, did something happen here?

steps.name: Ursine Worker
steps.text: *sigh* This young lady here fell and broke her pocket watch.

steps.name: Ursine Worker
steps.text: Her father... Li'l Letov, was the best watchmaker in town. He died this morning under a collapsed beam in their house. It's what he left her.
The young woman nods and drops to her knees to get on the same level as the little girl. She reaches her right hand out, and dusts off the girl's dirty clothes.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Yana, right? Can I call you Yanushka?

steps.name: Ursine Girl
steps.text: ...Mhm.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I remember you. You were so brave during the evacuation. You aren't crying just because of the broken watch, right?

steps.name: Ursine Girl
steps.text: Papa... died. Our home... is gone.

steps.name: Ursine Girl
steps.text: I don't know... where we can go...

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Perhaps none of us know...

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: But we need to keep walking until we find our new home.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: ...Go back, Milana. Your leg hasn't completely healed. This is far enough.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Leithanien is very far, Tulin. I don't know if this might be the last time we see each other.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Maybe it will be... but that place is free of the Ursine military police. I will be able to study and create in peace again, for a while.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Yes, I hear they have towering spires, taller than even the clouds. And their magic and music can bring warmth to even the coldest nights.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: But I don't need warmth. I need to find that spark of fire for the people.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: I can feel Ursus's harsh cold, but I don't know how to strike at its source... Just like my brother... I can only go to see more, and see for myself all the suffering faces across the lands.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: To me, Leithanien isn't a punishment. I will tear up all those arrogant scriptures, and turn even their most complicated spells into language that the workers can understand, to bring an end to this cold once and for all.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: A language that even I can understand?

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Haha, you're right... Milana, as a friend, I have one earnest request.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: After I'm gone, I want to entrust everyone here—all the miners coughing up blood in the mines, and all the children looking for bread in the snow fields, I entrust them to you.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: ...Tulin, are you kidding me? I'm not like you. I'm an ordinary woman.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: No, I'm an ordinary man myself. Every great person out there is actually as ordinary as can be.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Greatness isn't a gift you are born with. It's simply the hope that numerous ordinary folk have placed in those who are willing to carry a burden.
He reaches his right hand out to Milana.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Promise me, Milana. Whether I come back with glory... or send back a broken, blood-soaked chapter... you must live.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Look after them in my place. Don't let them simply bear with the pain. Let them grow roots in the pain.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Tulin... Will I... ever see you again?

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: As long as I'm still alive, I will do whatever I can to write back.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: But the moment we must part ways has come.

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: Goodbye, my dear friend...

steps.name: Ivan Tulin
steps.text: If we will never see dawn again, then light up each and every cold night in your own way.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: A lot of times, the roads that we walk are slippery and full of potholes. Even the most incredible men are bound to stumble and fall.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: That's not our fault. The fault lies with the place where we run and stand.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: It's just like how your papa could fix all kinds of pocket watches, but if a watch's shell was bent, then your papa wouldn't be able to fix it, no matter how much he polished its parts.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: All we can do is find a new shell and fit it with parts and make it better than the original. Your papa would be so proud, if you managed to do that.
Milana finishes and lifts her head to find the workers slowly gathering around her and the two children.
All of them are listening intently, with some of them fighting back tears.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Yanushka, everyone... Today, you have no choice but to leave your homes—

steps.name: Helpless Civilian
steps.text: Help... Just what is going on?

steps.name: Helpless Civilian
steps.text: There are bombs falling from the sky, and the whole town is crawling with monsters—

steps.name: Helpless Civilian
steps.text: Why... What happened to the army? Have they given up on this place, on protecting us?

steps.name: Helpless Civilian
steps.text: Bozhe moi... We've been abandoned again...

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Why wait for anyone to save us?

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Why do you always need to rely on others for protection? Why must you keep indulging in the city's false spring?

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Don't you have the same strength as those high and mighty men with big names?
Standing atop ruins of the recent past, the white-haired Liberi peers down—Those who are unwilling to leave their homes are gathered in front of her, listening to her speech.
Among them are workers, soldiers, the elderly, and children... Faces you see in just about every city in Ursus. They are confused. They are strong.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Friends of Zelgrad. You have my praise for your resilience and my compliments for your bravery.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: But, esteemed friends, do you know which words the empire uses to describe you? 'Restrained,' 'kind,' 'obedient.' Yes...

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: They kissed you on your foreheads and branded them with the words 'restrained.'

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: They drained your blood and poured 'kindness' into your veins.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: They inflicted your bodies and souls with weariness to make you 'obedient' and easy to bend to their will.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Under the banner of equality, they bestowed upon you equal destitution. And with hatred and envy, they traded for your love of life and courage in the face of fate.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: More importantly, they sealed your lips and made you ashamed to speak that sacred word—strength.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Yes, 'strength.' Something that should be abundant in your lives.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: For they know that once you think you have strength, you will crush their extravagant palaces and smash their authority.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: People of Ursus, you can do this—

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: ...If you want me to do this, Auntie, then I will.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I will make them believe, and my voice will reach them... throughout Ursus, and to Grypherburg.

steps.name: Grand Duchess Elisabeth
steps.text: Yes, dear Nastya. Watch them. They are waiting for you.
The noble princess nods slightly and begins walking down the stairs to the starving men gathered below.

The men are haggard and weary. They are starved to the point that they can't even lift their heads, and their hunched backs appear slight in the darkness. Right now, there is only one thing on their minds—
'Yurodstvo.'
Once, they willingly endured, but now they have desire. Yet before any of them can voice their wishes, a peaceful, unquestionable voice rings out.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: My suffering brothers and sisters, people of Ursus... I have returned.
The voice sounds the same to every one of its listeners, as though it is capable of cleansing the lands of all injustice and bringing salvation to all suffering.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I see your tears have run dry, yet you still cry out for mercy.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I see your bodies are covered with scars, yet you still crawl forward in the mud.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Until this day, when you finally look upon me—the Grand Princess of Ursus.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: And I shall declare to you the meaning of patience.
All of a sudden, there are bread, cheese, and cured meat... as if they have fallen from the sky.

Everyone in attendance forces themselves to lift their heads and reach their hands out. Though they are battered and bruised, not a single voice carries resentment. The only thing that can be heard is thunderous applause: 'Long live the Princess.'
Each of them clasps their hands for the Yurodstvo.
The Grand Duchess looks to the top of her castle and nods.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Children of Ursus, hear me...

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I see your teary eyes—

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: There is no need to wail simply because your wounds are torn asunder. It will wash away the dust coating your souls.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Do not curse the arrival of your suffering. It will open the door to eternity for you.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Your suffering will from now on be your sustenance. It will bring you boundless strength.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Use this strength to repay those who took joy in your suffering.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: There will come a day when we deserve these hardships we suffer, which we will use to measure the weight of our lives.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: But we will never sing the praises of our suffering. We willingly let our suffering fade away, because no one should be born to suffer.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: All of us will die, but if you will allow me, I guarantee to all of you a brief, transient happiness while you yet walk among the living.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Everything will take a turn for the better. Everything will be etched into your flesh and blood. Each bloody trail you leave in the snow is a red carpet that leads directly to our holy dominion.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Do you hear that? Your souls are calling out to you. They are screaming, thirsting for pillage and conquest.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: We will endure no longer. Every show of tolerance is an act of suicide. After all, the only thing that stands eternal above this field of permafrost is the truth that strength reigns supreme.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Now come with me. We will be the vanguard that opens the way.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: As long as we cut open a small crack on the surface of the ice, the surging waters within will wash away our shackles.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: The bread that fills our stomachs is but an insignificant manifestation of power.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: I will make Ursus spread her arms wide. The empire's embrace will be a place where tears are no longer shed.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: The future that I see has no golden idols or noble masters. Only the strong will walk side-by-side.

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Now go. You are the thunderclaps of this storm. Let our will bring order to Ursus!

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Once these seeds break through the snow, the wilderness will be white no longer. This is a future where we won't need to be given bread, a future where we all work the fields for one another.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: We will no longer be lonely seeds, but field upon field of golden wheat. That day will surely come, just as the sun will rise tomorrow—

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: Come, Ursines. Follow in the footsteps of your forebears.

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: In my eyes, you already stand...

steps.name: Anastasia
steps.text: ...in the kingdom of heaven.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Alright, Oleg is gone too. Ship's all clear!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Operation manual, control panel...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Gah, what a pain.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Let's see...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...Looks like there's a reason why this big girl needs a crew of eight just to keep her trudging along.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But that's just fine. If it's a suicide mission, we don't need a full complement.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: As long as we tune the presets right—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Command, right? Any further instructions?

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: ...back...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oh, I almost forgot. We've been coasting along for some time since we entered stealth mode. Soon, we'll be out of maximum comms range.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: If we can't hear each other, then I'll hang up.

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: In position...

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: ...Sechin, all units...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I can't make that out. You want all Sechin units to report back? That's easy. I'll be right there.

steps.name: Intermittent Voice
steps.text: ...Razin—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Is that 'all units?' Can't say for sure.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But we can at least return the Volnov in one piece. That's bringing everything to a proper conclusion.

spans.text: the Volnov in one piece. That's bringing everything to a proper conclusion.

steps.text: The young man follows the figures in the operation manual and adjusts the buttons and knobs on the control panel one-by-one, taking momentary pauses to observe the corresponding readings.
Once everything is ready and confirmed, he lifts the protective cover and presses the button underneath to lock down on the driving mode.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Ship's log, record. January 22, 1102. The Volnov will turn around in an empty field and sail full speed ahead.

spans.text: will turn around in an empty field and sail full speed ahead.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Our objective: The flagship of the Fourth Army's main fleet.
